claims.text: At stage-2 ProductsController takes DonHangDbContext; List filters db.Products by maxPriceVnd and orders by Id itself. Product (Domain/Entities.cs) and DonHangDbContext are declared public.

At stage-3 DonHang.Catalog declares 9 types: public ICatalog, CatalogProduct (record), CatalogModule; internal Product, CatalogDbContext, EfProductRepository, IProductRepository, ProductCache, CatalogService. No InternalsVisibleTo in the repository.

C#: an internal type is accessible only within the same assembly (the DLL its project builds); code in another project that names it fails to compile (CS0122). A public type is usable from any project that references its project.

ICatalog declares ListAsync(limit, offset, maxPriceVnd), FindAsync(id), ChangePriceAsync(id, priceVnd), all returning CatalogProduct values (null when no product has the id); CatalogProduct(Id, Name, PriceVnd).

CatalogService implements ICatalog: ListAsync queries CatalogDbContext (price filter, id order); FindAsync/ChangePriceAsync use IProductRepository = ProductCache wrapping EfProductRepository; results built as CatalogProduct. AddCatalogModule registers ICatalog as CatalogService.
At stage-3 ProductsController's constructor takes only ICatalog; List calls ListAsync and maps to ProductDto; Get calls FindAsync and UpdatePrice calls ChangePriceAsync.
C#: a public method cannot have a return type or parameter type less accessible than itself (e.g. internal); this is a compile error (inconsistent accessibility, CS0050/CS0051).

git grep -n -E <pattern> <tree> -- <path> searches the blobs of the given tree (such as a tag) instead of the working tree, with a POSIX extended regex, and prefixes each matching line with its line number.

Catalog can change its table mapping or cache without touching any caller as long as its public types (ICatalog, CatalogProduct and CatalogModule) stay the same; a change to those is the kind you plan with callers.

Between modules of one process a contract of C# types fits; an HTTP contract fits when the other side runs in another process, and inside one process it adds turning values into JSON and back, and network failures.
Making every type public lets other modules come to depend on a module's inside, so a storage change in one module can break another; keeping the inside internal prevents that.
